scenarios.title: Anyone with the app's public key can read every order
scenarios.narrative: The app ships a public 'anon' key to every browser by design. Before the fix, that key could read the whole orders table: names, emails, addresses, order history. During the private pilot that meant 12 testers' data; at public launch it would have meant every customer's data, findable by automated scanners without any targeted attack.

actions.outcome: public.orders denies anonymous reads and writes; verified by an independent re-probe, not by the original warning disappearing.

deadline.rationale: Anon-readable customer data at public launch is a critical contextual risk (rsk-anon-orders-public); during the pilot it is already high.

state_history.note: Read aspect verified by att-rls-migration-1 evidence; write aspect split into act-verify-anon-write.

procedures.title: Enable RLS with owner-only policies via a committed migration
prerequisites: Supabase CLI linked to the pilot project
Review of intended access rules with the founder
required_inputs: Table list and ownership column (user_id) for each private table

authorization.scope: Commit a migration on a branch and deploy it to the PILOT project only; production untouched.
authorization.notes: Diff shown to the founder before deploy; branch-first.

steps: Write migration: alter table public.orders enable row level security; create owner-only select/insert/update policies keyed on auth.uid() = user_id.
Open a branch + PR with the diff; get founder/developer sign-off.
Run the verification provider (prc-write-probe / read re-probe) for fresh evidence.

failure_behavior.on_failure: Migration fails closed: RLS enable without policies denies all access rather than exposing data; app errors surface in the pilot only.
failure_behavior.rollback: Revert the migration commit and redeploy; policies are dropped by the down migration.

procedures.success_evidence: Deployed migration visible in project history AND independent re-probe shows anon read denied on a non-empty table.
